XYZ.thesis_one_line: Payments and Cash App lender growing gross profit 25% with raised guidance, priced for less growth than I expect, but a DOJ matter and rising loan losses remain.
kill_criteria: Transaction, loan and consumer-receivable losses above 22% of gross profit in any quarter (Q2'26: 18.5%; source: 10-Q/10-K statement of operations, Block consolidated).
Total DOJ resolution (payment or further accrual) above $1.0B (10-Q Note 16 accrual at 30 Jun 2026: $526M).
Quarterly gross profit growth below 12% YoY for two consecutive quarters (Q3'26 guide: +18%).
FY26 Adjusted Diluted EPS guide cut below $3.85 (the May 2026 level) at any release.
Cash and cash equivalents (consolidated, balance sheet) below $4.0B before the 1 Nov 2027 convertible maturity without new financing.
key_adverse_facts: DOJ inquiry unresolved: company accrued $526M at Q2'26 and says losses in excess of the accrual 'could be material' (10-Q 30 Jun 2026, Note 16).
Transaction, loan and consumer-receivable losses $585.5M in Q2'26 vs $294.1M (+99%), 18.5% of gross profit vs 11.6%, against gross profit +25%.
Securities class action (filed 17 Jan 2025) survived motion to dismiss on 6 Jan 2026; derivative suits and a special litigation committee (April 2026).

TTM GAAP EPS about $0.56 vs TTM adjusted EPS $3.06; adjusted measures exclude legal/regulatory accruals ($743M Q1'26, $365M Q2'26 'contingencies, restructuring and other charges') and H1'26 restructuring of $495.0M.
Full-year guide implies H2'26 gross profit growth of about 16% vs 25% in Q2; Q3'26 guide +18%.
data_conflicts: Yahoo FCF about -$27M vs company non-GAAP TTM FCF $3.88B: customer-loan originations are classed as investing and credit-loss provisions are added back in operating cash flow.
Yahoo sharesOutstanding 540.8M is Class A only; total Class A + B is 600.8M at 30 Jun 2026.
Triage Q06 regulatory figures (CFPB, NY DFS, multistate AML) not independently opened; only the 10-Q items were verified.
XYZ.next_earnings_date_basis: announced in the Q2'26 shareholder letter (8-K 0001193125-26-335117); corrected by DV45 2026-10-09
XYZ.confidence_in_thesis: medium (strong operating beats and three guidance raises, but adjusted earnings exclude recurring legal costs and the DOJ outcome is open)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Reverse DCF on $2.1B normalised owner earnings (15% haircut to FY26 adjusted EPS guide) implies 8.3% ten-year growth at a 10% cost of equity versus my 10.2% base.

XYZ.scenario_basis: Start FY26 adjusted EPS $4.02 (guide), no dividend; bear 4% growth and 11x exit, base 15% growth and 16x exit, bull 22% growth and 19x exit; from $76.42 over 3 years.

GRMN.thesis_one_line: Debt-free maker of sport watches, marine and aviation gear with raised guidance, but the share price already assumes faster growth than this business can likely sustain.
kill_criteria: Consolidated revenue growth below 5% YoY for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26: +11%).
Fitness segment revenue down YoY in any quarter (Q2'26: +25%).
Consolidated gross margin (ex tariff refunds, per 10-Q MD&A) below 57.0% for two quarters (Q2'26 ex-refund about 61.4%).
FY26 pro forma EPS guidance cut below the $10.00 set on 29 Jul 2026.
Inventories above 30% of trailing-twelve-month revenue at any quarter end (27 Jun 2026: $1,966M / TTM revenue $7.67B = 25.6%).
key_adverse_facts: Reverse DCF implies about 11% ten-year FCF growth vs my base of about 5.8%. [Corrected 2026-10-08 DV19: at a 9.67% rate, with interest income removed from FCF and SBC deducted, about 13-15%.]
Q2'26 gross margin of 62.4% includes about $21M (about 100 bps) of one-time IEEPA tariff refunds (10-Q).
Fitness +32% in H1'26 while Outdoor is -3%; Q2'26 revenue growth of 11% was the slowest of the last four quarters; guidance implies H2'26 pro forma EPS growth of about 7%.
Inventories $1,966M vs $1,772M at 27 Dec 2025 (+11%) and Q2 capex $127.8M vs $45.7M.
P/E 29.4x FY26 pro forma EPS guide of $10.00; FCF yield 2.8%.
data_conflicts: Yahoo totalDebt $227M is lease liabilities; the 27 Jun 2026 balance sheet shows no borrowings.
Yahoo FCF $1.04B vs my TTM FCF of $1.60B (OCF less capex, four quarters to Q2'26).
b1 ranks GRMN 336th on stale 29 Apr 2026 filing data; the quality/surprise strength in b1 is momentum-driven.
GRMN.next_earnings_date_basis: estimated from prior-year date 2025-10-29; not announced in filings
GRMN.confidence_in_thesis: medium (business quality is high and guidance conservative; the issue is valuation, not fundamentals)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. EV $52.4B on $1.65B forward FCF implies 11.0% ten-year growth at a 9% WACC versus my 5.8% base, so a great business priced for more than it can deliver. [Corrected 2026-10-08 DV19: at 9.67% implied is 12.6%; with interest income removed from FCF and SBC deducted about 15.1%; implied_vs_base above, verdict unchanged.]

GRMN.scenario_basis: Start FY26 pro forma EPS $10.00 (guide), dividends $4.20 a year; bear 3% growth and 18x exit, base 8% growth and 24x exit, bull 12% growth and 28x exit; from $294.14 over 3 years.

CPT.thesis_one_line: Sunbelt apartment landlord selling California at a high price to buy Sunbelt homes and its own shares, but rents are still falling and debt is elevated.
kill_criteria: Same-property NOI growth (ex-California) worse than -2.0% YoY for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26: -1.4%; source: earnings supplement "Same Property Results").
Net debt to annualised Adjusted EBITDAre (consolidated, supplement) above 5.0x at both the Q3'26 and Q4'26 reports (Q2'26: 5.3x).
FY26 Core FFO guidance midpoint cut below $6.50 (current $6.75).
Blended same-property lease-rate growth below -2.0% for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26: -0.2%; Q1'26: -1.6%).
Same-property occupancy below 94.5% in any quarter (Q2'26: 95.7%).
key_adverse_facts: Same-property NOI (ex-California) fell 1.4% in Q2'26 after 0.0%, 0.0% and -0.7% in prior quarters; new-lease rates -3.3%.
Net debt to annualised Adjusted EBITDAre 5.3x in Q2'26 vs 4.2x a year earlier; total debt $4,848M vs $3,826M.
Bought back 4.06M shares at an average $104.08 in H1'26, above the $98.12 close.
$53.0M revenue-management-software class-action settlement (excluded from Core FFO); 2026 Core FFO excludes about $0.63 a share of non-core charges.
Core FFO midpoint held at $6.75 but below FY25 actual $6.88; same-property NOI guidance midpoint now (0.60)% ex-California.
data_conflicts: Yahoo forward EPS $1.09 and P/E 90x are GAAP figures distorted by property gains; 2026 GAAP EPS guide of $9.76-$10.10 includes the California sale gain.
Yahoo share count 100.5M vs 103.9M common and common-equivalent shares in the Q2'26 supplement (includes operating-partnership units).
b1 quality score (0.80) is a GAAP-ratio artefact; Core AFFO $5.90 in FY25 is the better cash measure.
CPT.next_earnings_date_basis: estimated from prior-year date 2025-11-06; not announced in filings
CPT.confidence_in_thesis: medium (capital allocation is credible; fundamentals have not yet turned)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Equity value $10.2B on $0.608B Core AFFO implies 2.3% ten-year growth at an 8.5% cost of equity versus my 2.5% base, so fairly priced with about 6.8% base total return below the hurdle.

CPT.scenario_basis: Start FY26 Core FFO $6.75 (guide midpoint), dividends $4.30 a year ($12.90 over 3 years); bear Core FFO $6.50 and 12.5x exit, base $7.35 and 14.5x, bull $7.70 and 17x; from $98.12 over 3 years.
